ci: the workspace row's last two reds -- stitch builds whole in release, and the maps archive-watcher test waits for its worker. The CI tests with --release, and release became incremental in the compile-time work: split into incremental codegen units, stitch's interpreter handlers no longer tail-call each other and makepad-script's math_aot aborted with a stack overflow (every run since d8f765668; it aborted rather than failed, so it was never in the failed list). [profile.release.package.makepad-stitch] incremental = false. map::view's archive_watcher_rejects_malformed_mbtiles_zoom_metadata gave the watcher thread 2000 x 1 ms; with every test binary running at once that was not enough, so it waits up to 30 s. Checked: cargo test --release for math_aot (19 pass, overflowed before) and the maps test

builder: every question sits in one place, and neither the Makepad nor the Rust license is asked for -- the email, the folder, the Rust choice and every other question were on the status line under the rule while the other choices were rows above it; now each is shown as rows at the end of the content above the rule (the question, then its options or its input row, the active one selected with the band and ▌), the line under the rule keeps messages and progress, the same in makepad.sh and the Windows TUI. Downloading the Builder already agrees to the Makepad commercial license (the site says so) and Rust's (MIT or Apache 2.0) asks for no acceptance, so the "Install build tools" consent before a first build and the Update consent are gone for them; the Agreements row says "✓ nothing to accept" and its page lists them to read ("applies by downloading", "nothing to accept"). Microsoft's build tools and SDK and NVIDIA's CUDA (Windows with local AI) keep their consent screen and Agree to all / Disagree. Escape in the shell now waits 50 ms for an arrow key's rest (bash 3.2 still a second), so Escape then an arrow cannot turn into an answer; a scroll hint with nothing above or below is not shown. Checked: cargo check (host, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, -msvc), the lib tests, both TUIs in a pty: the log-in page, a yes/no question, the email prompt, the Agreements page and row
